# Gödel — Formally Undecidable Propositions (1931)

## Bibliographic identity

Original German article metadata and text are verified. The exact English wording of Satz VI and Satz XI remains deferred until a selected lawful translation is consulted.

## Chicago 18 forms

**Original bibliography:** Gödel, Kurt. “Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze der Principia Mathematica und verwandter Systeme I.” *Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik* 38 (1931): 173–98. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01700692.

**Full note:** Kurt Gödel, “Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze der *Principia Mathematica* und verwandter Systeme I,” *Monatshefte für Mathematik und Physik* 38 (1931): {page/note}, https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01700692.

**Shortened note:** Gödel, “Über formal unentscheidbare Sätze,” {page/note}.

## Essay use

Primary theorem source for precise internal limits on consistent, effectively axiomatized formal systems sufficiently expressive for arithmetic. It supports neither a generic “everything is incomplete” claim nor a proof that mind, God, QL, or the subject transcends computation.

**Passages available:** short primary German context and scope excerpts are contained in the passage cards below. A fixed English translation of Satz VI and Satz XI remains a deferred burden; `raatikainen-2026-godel-incompleteness-sep` supplies a separate current technical scope source.
